title: Vesper and the Protocol
premise: Silas Brightwater, a clone who inherited the original's unsolved murder case, keeps the beacon no one remembers commissioning. When a name appears on a ship's manifest that never flew, Silas and the stranger it names—Vesper, who has no memory of her own—are drawn into a conspiracy to weaponize the beacon's signal against the relay at dead space's edge. Racing the closing jump window, they discover the original Brightwater was murdered for uncovering the Protocol, and that Vesper is its living key. In the end, Silas must choose between preserving his inherited identity and erasing himself alongside the Protocol, while Vesper chooses to remember.
about_author: August Thornbury is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing maintenance logs before turning them into fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write about people who keep things running that everyone else forgot.

chapters.title: The Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Silas maintains the beacon alone, haunted by the original's murder file he inherited along with his face. A routine manifest audit surfaces an impossible entry: Vesper, listed on a vessel never registered. When she arrives at the station with no memory and a beacon access code tattooed on her wrist, Silas realizes someone sent her here deliberately. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: wary curiosity hardening into dread.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rising
chapters.summary: Vesper's fragmented memories surface in dreams that match details from the murder file, suggesting she knew the original Brightwater. Decoding the beacon reveals the Protocol: a directive to convert the relay into a memory-erasure weapon controlled by whoever holds the jump window. The conspirators who killed the original trace their access attempt and lock down the station. POV: alternating Silas and Vesper. Emotional beat: found-family tenderness blooming under threat.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: With hours before the window closes, Silas and Vesper steal a derelict tug and run the gauntlet toward the relay, pursued by Protocol loyalists. Vesper recovers the crucial memory: she was the Protocol's designer who chose to forget rather than let it be used. The loyalists offer Silas the original's complete memories as bait. POV: Vesper, then Silas. Emotional beat: terror and sacrifice colliding at the edge of dead space.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: At the relay, Silas confronts the Protocol's architect—the original's killer—and refuses the offered memories, choosing his own imperfect self over inherited truth. Vesper broadcasts the beacon's true purpose, overwriting the weapon directive with the archive of everyone the Protocol erased. The window closes with the loyalists stranded; Silas and Vesper remain as the beacon's new keepers, family by choice. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging.
